reason: Checked against the code; both gaps are real. tools/trainlab.py l.731-745 takes t* as the argmax over the non-control arms only (arms_dc leaves out DC_CONTROL = 0.25). So the pre-registered rule 'Если t* = 0.25, сборки нет' (TASK_CLOUD_SESSION.md l.178) can never fire, and an arm that lost to the control on SELECTION can still become t*. The neighbours of t* are grid[k-1] and grid[k+1] where they exist. At t* = 0.15 the plateau is checked on one side only (0.20). At t* = 0.20 it always fails, because conf_of[0.25] is 0.0 by definition. L2 (in force) adds t* < 0.25, which rules out 0.30 and 0.35. So the gate in force (strict plateau AND L2) can pass only at 0.15, and there its plateau check is weakest. That is also the one threshold with a negative public prior: sjlee101's fork with DeepCenter safe-div 0.20->0.15 scored 0.946, against 0.947 for both 0.20 and 0.25 (CONTEXT l.699-703). Value: the fix only tightens the gate and restores the pre-registered meaning ('both neighbouring thresholds'; the control counts as a candidate). It is offline lab code, so it touches no kernel, byte-identity or runtime. It also follows the L2 precedent: a bug fix plus tightening needs no user OK. Timing: exp60 holds only results_forkblob.* on disk, and the T9 main score was still 'running' (CONTEXT l.1923, checked 20:25 UTC). So it can still land before any DeepCenter number is read. Caveats, and the reason this is not a big win. (1) Once the '2 neighbours' clause is added, strict plus L2 cannot pass at ANY t*: 0.15 is at the grid edge, 0.20 has the control as a neighbour, and 0.30/0.35 are above the control. So in practice this closes K3b until the user gives the OK for L1. It must be recorded as that closure, not dressed up as a small bug fix. Under L1 plus the 2-neighbour clause, only t* = 0.20 can pass, and it needs 0.15 >= +0.001. (2) The expected private gain is small. T9 already discounts network-confidence arcs to 0. Round 1 (d3 value) put K3b's ceiling at a handful of fork events. R4 still asks public >= +0.002 before F1. So this mostly prevents a false-pass K3b dummy plus one S5 slot, rather than moving the private score.
fix: Make these changes in tools/trainlab.py gates(), before any exp60 T9 DeepCenter number is read. (1) Compute sel_ctrl = 0.0. Set tstar = 0.25 (control) unless max(sel over non-control) > 0; a tie or a None goes to the control. Add the check 'sel_t_star_gt_control': sel[best] is not None and sel[best] > 0. (2) Add the check 'two_grid_neighbours': len(neigh) == 2. AND both checks into pass_strict, pass_noncontrol_plateau, pass_strict_plateau_L2 and pass_noncontrol_plateau_L2, and keep the old booleans as 'old_*' fields so results.md prints the old and new verdicts side by side. (3) Make decisions_text say explicitly: 'in force (strict + L2 + 2-neighbour) is structurally unpassable for every grid t*; K3b builds only after the user's OK for L1, and then only at t* = 0.20 with conf(0.15) >= +0.001'. (4) Add one CONTEXT line (dated, before T9 is read): 'PRE-REG v3 ADDENDUM L2b [bug fix + tightening, no OK needed]: t* = argmax over the grid including the control (sel 0); a grid-edge t* has no two-sided plateau -> no build; consequence: K3b is closed under the rules in force until L1 is OK'd; S5 planned empty'. Do not add a 0.10 arm or any other new arm now (more selection after the fact). Add a unit test with synthetic agg dicts for t* = 0.15 (edge, fail), 0.20 (strict fail, L1 pass if conf(0.15) >= 0.001), and all sel < 0 (control, no build). Also wrap the new gate code fail-soft, or at least make sure a missing aggregate gives False, not a vacuous True.
realistic_gain: Private score: about +0 to +1e-4 expected. It removes the one path where the gate in force could pass: t* = 0.15, with a one-sided plateau and a negative public prior (0.946 vs 0.947). Operationally it saves a K3b dummy (~0.7 GPU-h) and an S5 LB slot in the false-pass branch (P ~0.1-0.2), and it keeps the gate honest and pre-registered. Cost is about 20-30 min of CPU-side code plus a test, with no kernel risk.
